 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Arch Manning's future in College Football remains a complete unknown as the Texas Longhorns head into this weekend's game against LSU. 
 Manning could declare for the 2027 NFL Draft, but there is also the distinct possibility that he could remain in college for another year, which could even see him move on from the Longhorns. As many debate whether the quarterback is ready for the NFL, one thing that Manning is not lacking is a good support group around him.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The 22-year-old threw three touchdowns and no interceptions last weekend against Missouri. Having enjoyed a much improved game, the Longhorns' QB was offered some advice from his uncle, Eli Manning.
 Eli Manning shares advice for nephew Arch Manning
 "Hey, you know, it's never going to be perfect. That's why you play the game. It's not always going to be smooth. Every game, every series is an opportunity to learn and get better," Manning said on ESPN.
 "And you've got to learn how to just take the ups and downs of a game. There are going to be a couple of series where you have a three-and-out. Hey, you're going to throw an interception, but you're also going to make some plays. And you can never let one series dictate your mindset going into the next one.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "I think he's done a good job overcoming those things and just bouncing back, always being present and being able to step up late in games and make the plays that he needs to make. So, he's still a young quarterback. He's learning each and every week. And I think they're playing well right now. He's in a good rhythm. Hopefully, they can keep that going."
 Manning has thrown seven interceptions this season, with two of them coming in the win in October against Ole Miss. However, the Longhorns' quarterback has been able to come through the last two games without throwing a single interception.
 There is still time for Manning to prove himself worthy of declaring for the upcoming draft, but there will also be no shame in the 22-year-old staying in the college game for another year to continue his development.
